decisions.reason: As a flagship cheese closely tied to the firm's strategic direction and core organic dairy offer, it is very likely to be retained unless there is a clear performance problem.

A semi-hard cheese wheel fits the firm's established cheese range well, and after several years on the market it likely serves as a stable assortment product rather than a candidate for quick withdrawal.
The mild creamy soft cheese broadens the portfolio in an accessible way and supports the firm's narrow but coherent organic cheese assortment, so keeping it is more likely than dropping it.

Although the washed-rind soft cheese remains the most niche of the surviving launches and is therefore the most exposed to assortment cleanup, its continued presence suggests enough fit with the firm's specialist dairy positioning to justify keeping it for now.
